svg.text: FIG 06: PURE LC RESONANT TANKS, VOLTAGE DOUBLING & DIODE COMMUTATION
Zero-Dissipation Energy Ping-Pong • 2 V_dc Peak Phenomenon • Natural Diode Commutation • Trapped Voltage States

g.text: When resistance R = 0, the circuit contains only conservative reactive elements.
Surge / Char. Imp: Z₀ = √(L / C) Ω
Z₀ relates peak inductor voltage and capacitor current amplitudes: V_peak = Z₀ · I_peak.
DC Step Excitation of Pure Series LC
An uncharged series LC tank (v_C(0⁻)=0, i_L(0⁻)=0) is connected to a DC source V_dc:
i(t) = (V_dc / Z₀) · sin(ω₀t) · u(t) = V_dc · √(C/L) · sin(ω₀t)
v_L(t) = V_dc - v_C(t) = V_dc · cos(ω₀t) · u(t)
Notice that v_C(t) oscillates sinusoidally about the source level V_dc with amplitude V_dc!
Total stored energy in the tank at any instant t:
v_C = V_dc, i = I_peak = V_dc / Z₀.
E_C = ½ C V_dc², E_L = ½ L (V_dc² C/L) = ½ C V_dc²
E_C = ½ C (2 V_dc)² = 2 C V_dc², E_L = 0
All energy is concentrated entirely in the capacitor's electric field!
The maximum occurs when cos(ω₀t) = -1, which happens at:
Capacitor charges to EXACTLY DOUBLE THE DC SUPPLY VOLTAGE!
This is an essential principle in pulse forming networks and resonant power supplies!
General Doubling with Initial Voltage V₀
If the capacitor already carries an initial voltage v_C(0⁻) = V₀:
v_{C,max} = V_dc + |V_dc - V₀| = 2V_dc - V₀ (if V₀ < V_dc)
Special High-Yield Exam Case: Initial V₀ = -V_dc
If initial voltage is opposite polarity V₀ = -V_dc:
Triple voltage peaking! Very frequent in circuit breaker restrike analysis.
• When current is MAXIMUM, capacitor voltage equals SOURCE voltage V_dc!
• When voltage is MAXIMUM (2 V_dc), loop current is ZERO!
• The voltage and current are 90° out of phase (pure reactive exchange).
Consider a series circuit with DC Source V_dc, ideal Diode D, inductor L,
and uncharged capacitor C. Switch closes at t = 0.
Phase 1: Conduction Interval 0 ≤ t ≤ π / ω₀
• Diode conducts forward current: i(t) = (V_dc / Z₀) · sin(ω₀t) > 0.
• Capacitor charges up following: v_C(t) = V_dc · (1 - cos ω₀t).
• At t = π / ω₀ = T₀ / 2, the current hits its first natural zero:
i(π / ω₀) = 0 A, v_C(π / ω₀) = 2 · V_dc
Phase 2: Natural Commutation & Turn-Off (t > π / ω₀)
• Current attempts to reverse (sin ω₀t < 0), but the DIODE BLOCKS IT!
• Diode turns OFF spontaneously (Natural / Resonant Commutation).
Peak Inverse Voltage (PIV) on the Diode:
With diode OFF and v_C = 2V_dc, KVL across diode gives:
• In SCR (Thyristor) resonant inverters and DC choppers (Jones chopper):
An auxiliary LC circuit forces the thyristor current to zero,
allowing the device to commutate without external forced shutoff.
Q_trans = ∫₀^{t_cond} i(t) dt = C · (2V_dc) = 2 · C · V_dc
Given: V_dc = 100 V, L = 10 mH, C = 40 μF, uncharged capacitor.
Diode D is ideal. Switch closes at t = 0.
Find: Conduction time, peak current, and final capacitor voltage.
Drill 2: LC Tank with Initial Pre-Charge
Given: V_dc = 50 V, L = 1 H, C = 1 F, initial v_C(0⁻) = 20 V.
Switch closes at t = 0 (no diode, pure LC loop).
i(t) = C · dv_C/dt = 1 · 30 · sin(t) = 30 · sin(t) A
Voltage swings between 20 V and 80 V with mean value 50 V!
In Drill 1 (Diode-LC), how much energy is SUPPLIED by the DC source V_dc
E_source = ∫₀^{t_cond} V_dc · i(t) dt = V_dc · Q_total
E_C(final) = ½ · C · [v_C(final)]² = ½ C (2V_dc)² = 2 · C · V_dc²
E_source = E_C(final)! ZERO ENERGY IS DISSIPATED (η = 100%)!
Contrast with RC charging which is ALWAYS 50% efficient!
